messages:
Ben H: Hey folks, noticed my July paystub withheld Canadian CPP/EI even though I'm a US-based contractor doing a 6-week engagement in Toronto. I thought short-term contractors weren't subject to CPP/EI by default?
Aria (People Ops): Thanks for flagging @Ben. Did you complete the contractor tax form for Canada or select a non-resident status in the vendor portal?
Ben H: I filled the cross-border contractor form and checked "non-resident short-term" in the portal. I also uploaded my US tax docs (W-9). Screenshot DM'ed.
Leo - Payroll: Thanks Ben 3I'm seeing the vendor feed included CAN jurisdiction lines and the payroll engine defaulted to employee-like withholding for CPP/EI because the vendor type was "employee-like contractor". That mapping can trigger CPP/EI unless TaxOps confirms non-resident exemption.
Ben H: Ugh. So will I get refunded? I don't want to have to claim it on my Canadian return.
Aria (People Ops): We'll need TaxOps to audit whether the CPP/EI was legally required. If it was withheld in error, payroll can process an off-cycle reversal and refund net. If it was correctly withheld, you may need to file Canada returns to claim refund as a non-resident.
Leo - Payroll: Quick technical note: our payroll tax vendor requires a jurisdiction flag + supporting doc (NR status). The cross-border form uploaded didn't sync the NR flag due to a metadata mismatch in the feed on 07/02. I'll request a feed re-sync and hold any remits.
TaxOps Bot: Case TAX-4822 opened by Leo - Payroll: "CPP/EI withheld for short-term US contractor - Ben H". ETA 4 business days for audit.
Aria (People Ops): Ben, we'll pause any remittance if possible and run the audit. If reversal is needed, it will be an off-cycle credit labeled "CPP/EI reversal - Ben H" and show on your next pay statement. Please watch for any mail from CRA and keep the DM'ed docs handy. :white_check_mark:
Ben H: Thanks. Appreciate the quick triage. If there's anything I need to file in the US to reconcile, let me know.
Leo - Payroll: If reversal happens, YTD federal will be unaffected; it's a jurisdictional payroll tax correction. We may need to adjust any employer-side remittance reconciliations if CRA already received a payment. We'll update TAX-4822 here when audit completes.
Aria (People Ops): Closing loop: we'll follow up in this thread once TAX-4822 is resolved. If anyone else is doing short international gigs, please DM HR before the pay cycle cutoff. :wave:
